_what: Which shape each §8 `S` cell takes, decided by RFC-2026-022 §3's test and recorded here rather than argued in each migration's header.
_why_this_file_exists_before_any_entry: RFC-2026-022 names this file, and four batches are about to classify cells at the same time. If each created it, the merge would be a four-way conflict over a file whose whole purpose is to be one list — so it is created once, empty, with the rules that read it.
Empty is a claim: no §8 `S` cell has been classified yet. The rules below make that claim checkable rather than merely true today.

_shape.cell: the §8 row and column this entry classifies, quoted from the access matrix
_shape.table: table name created by a migration in db/foundation/migrations/, schema-qualified as `app.<name>` or `private.<name>`; an unqualified name means `app`
_shape.why: which half of RFC-2026-022 §3's test the STATEMENT falls on, in a sentence someone can disagree with
_shape.batch: the migration batch that classified it

_not_in_effect: RFC-2026-022 is approved and NOT IN EFFECT: measured 2026-09-08, the only member of app_worker is postgres, which bypasses RLS. A batch classifies its cells here; it does not write a service policy until §7 holds.
_what_batch_110_classified: Batch 110 classifies one cell here: §8.3's "Raw token/webhook SELECT", which RFC-2026-022 §3's own table assigns to batches 110 and 131 and calls DISCOVERED. 131 owns the same cell for the payment inbox and adds its own row; the register keys on (cell, statement), so two rows for one cell on two tables is the shape §5/1 describes rather than a duplicate.
_a_private_table_needed_the_rule_to_say_: The `table` field was documented as "unqualified table name in the app schema", and this cell's table is in `private` — §3.1 puts "raw webhook" there by name and §14's gate checklist requires it not be exposed. The rule could not express the entry it was written to receive. It now accepts a schema-qualified name and resolves an unqualified one to `app`, which changes no verdict for a cell in `app` and is asserted in test-kits/db/foundation-contract.test.mjs in both directions.

cells.why: The statement a processor issues is "the next unprocessed delivery", and it contains no workspace term because WHICH workspace is what reading the row resolves. Under RFC-2026-022 §3's operational test, adding the confinement term to its WHERE does not narrow the same work — it turns "the unprocessed webhook" into "the unprocessed webhook of a tenant I already knew", which is not the work. The schema says the same thing: private.meta_webhook_inbox.workspace_id is NULLABLE, because a delivery arrives before anything knows whose it is and resolution can fail, and batch 110's apply-time block refuses a later NOT NULL.
